description: Production startup validates manifest, hashes, tensor contracts, architecture, and policy before spawning the worker

gates.description: Model manifest (packaging/model-manifest.toml) is parsed at startup
ModelSpec entries are built from the manifest with real sha256 hashes (no zero hashes)
All-zero sha256 in a manifest variant is rejected pre-spawn
ModelSpec.sha256 that does not match the manifest variant sha256 is rejected
On-disk model file whose sha256 does not match the manifest is rejected (tamper detection)
Manifest tensor contract is structurally validated (non-empty shapes, known dtype)
Manifest target_arch is validated against the current CPU architecture
Redistribution policy is enforced: restricted models require authorisation
All three bundled models (yunet_2023mar, sface_2021dec, minifasnet_pad) pass validation in sequence
The real packaging/model-manifest.toml validates against the real bundled ONNX models on disk
Startup validation log messages contain model_id and sha256 but no frames, embeddings, templates, pixels, or scores
Seccomp sandbox denies open syscall — ONNX Runtime cannot open model files after sandbox is applied
Seccomp sandbox denies socket syscall — worker cannot open network connections
Real ONNX Runtime CPU inference round-trip for all three bundled models (hardware-gated)

model_paths.description: Model files are stored as <models_dir>/<id>.onnx (FP32) or <models_dir>/<id>_int8.onnx (INT8). Per-model metadata (licence records, sha256 sidecars) lives in <models_dir>/<id>/ subdirectory. Previous flat/subdirectory ambiguity is resolved.

startup_sequence: 2. Resolve required model IDs → ModelSpecs with real sha256 from manifest
3. For each model: validate zero-hash → spec-hash-match → tensor-contract → architecture → file-hash → admission → policy
5. Any validation fails → fail closed (no worker spawn)

ModelFetcher::validate_against_manifest() for each model before spawn
